title: The specificity problem, and the Cre/lox trick
objective: Explain why labeling or manipulating one cell type is hard, and how Cre recombinase + loxP solves it.

steps.title: The whole game: change one cell type, not the whole mouse
steps.body: Almost every question in the lab starts the same way: *these* neurons — not their neighbors, not the rest of the body. Mouse genetics is how you get that specificity. If you can't restrict a label or a manipulation to one population, you can't attribute anything you see to it.

steps.title: Cre = scissors, loxP = 'cut here' marks
steps.body:
**[[Cre]]** is an enzyme (a recombinase) that recognizes short 34-bp DNA tags called **[[loxP]]** sites. When two loxP sites point the same way, Cre **excises** the DNA between them. DNA flanked by loxP is said to be **'floxed'** (flanked-by-loxP).

Mental model: Cre is scissors; loxP sites are the dotted 'cut here' lines.

visual.alt: Cre cuts at the two loxP sites flanking a STOP cassette; the STOP is excised and the downstream payload gene switches on.
visual.caption: Cre cuts at loxP → STOP removed → the gene switches on.

steps.prompt: What does Cre do when it finds two loxP sites in the same orientation?
steps.explanation: Same-orientation loxP sites → excision of the intervening DNA. (If the loxP sites are inverted, Cre flips the sequence instead — that's the basis of [[DIO]]/FLEX viral tools, later.)

variants.setup: Cre finds two loxP sites in the same orientation flanking a STOP cassette.
variants.reveal: Same-orientation loxP leads to excision (deletion); opposite-orientation loxP would invert the DNA instead.

steps.title: Two mice make it specific
steps.body:
Specificity comes from a **two-part system**:

- **Driver line** — `Gene-Cre`: Cre is made only in cells that normally express `Gene` (e.g. *Bmpr1b-Cre* → Cre only in Bmpr1b+ neurons).
- **Responder line** — a payload (a fluorophore, a [[DREADD]], a toxin) sits behind a **floxed STOP** cassette, silent until Cre removes the STOP.

Cross them, and only the cells that make Cre switch the payload on.

steps.setup: You cross Bmpr1b-Cre with a floxed-STOP-tdTomato [[reporter]]. In the offspring, which cells glow red?
options: No cells — you need a drug too
steps.reveal: Only Bmpr1b+ cells make Cre, so only they delete the STOP and express tdTomato. Everything else stays dark. That restriction — one gene's expression pattern defining the labeled cells — is the core of the whole toolkit.

variants.prompt: In a Bmpr1b-Cre mouse carrying a floxed-STOP reporter, which cells light up?
variants.explanation: Cre is made only where the Bmpr1b promoter is active, so only those cells recombine and express the reporter.

sources.citation: Cre/lox is standard molecular genetics; see Principles of Neural Science (Kandel et al.) for background.

reviewNotes: Foundational. Inverted-loxP (flip) is previewed here and reused in C3/C5 DIO tools.
